slides.title: Content engineering path
slides.subtitle: Images, video, audio

content.whyBenefit: After this module you will create images, short videos and audio with AI – from a clear brief to quality and rights checks.
content.heroSubText: For marketing and communication specialists – visual and audio content with AI.
content.firstActionCTA: In 1–2 minutes open one image tool (e.g. ChatGPT with DALL·E or Ideogram) and generate one image from your description.
outcomes: You will understand a 6-step media chain – from the task brief to a check before publishing
You will keep the same product or style across a series and plan sound before cuts
You will know what to measure and what to check before publishing (rights, AI label)

sections.heading: In short
sections.body: Before you generate an image or clip, pick a campaign goal: Awareness, Engagement or Conversion. The diagram links the goal to the visual.

sections.heading: Campaign goals diagram
sections.body: Pick a goal – each band shows what to emphasize: emotion at the top, clarity at the bottom.
sections.imageAlt: Campaign goals funnel: Awareness, Engagement, Conversion

sections.heading: Do this now
sections.body: Think of one real post or ad. Tap the matching band in the diagram, then copy the template below and fill it in (or run it in AI).

sections.heading: Campaign goals: how to decide
sections.body: Awareness – attention and emotion; typical: cover, banner, social post. Engagement – context and stop-scroll; typical: carousel, video intro, illustration. Conversion – action, product, call to action (CTA); typical: ad layout, landing hero, “buy now” block. When emotion vs clarity: Awareness often = emotion; Conversion = clarity and trust.

sections.heading: Copyable template
sections.body: Paste into an AI chat or fill it yourself – pick A/E/C for your visual.
sections.copyable:
Goal (A/E/C): [awareness / engagement / conversion].
Context: [product], platform [where], audience [who].
Reply: 1) one goal, 2) what to emphasize visually (emotion / context / CTA), 3) 1 format.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Do you have one clear A/E/C goal and a one-sentence “why” (from the template / AI)? If not – go back to the bands or the template. If yes – continue to the Media chain.

sections.heading: Where to use this
sections.body: Marketing visuals, social images and short videos, background music or sounds for projects – without needing a designer or composer every time.

slides.title: Generative media chain
slides.subtitle: From the brief to a check – 6 steps without expensive guesswork

sections.heading: In short
sections.body: You win with a clear work chain (from brief to check), not the “best model”. One prompt straight into video often means expensive retries – lock the plan, frames and reference photos first, then short clips, audio and a check.

sections.heading: Chain diagram
sections.body: 6 steps – tap a stage. For the business cycle (brief → A/B) see the slide “Workflow: from brief to publication”.
sections.imageAlt: Generative media chain: brief, frames, refs, I2V, audio, check

sections.heading: Why these 6 steps
sections.body: The six diagram steps are the technical spine. The checklist below is practice for your topic (not a second step list).

sections.heading: Do this now
sections.body: Fill the checklist for your topic – this is a plan, not a generator prompt.

sections.heading: Copyable template
sections.body: Chain checklist – copy and fill it in.
sections.copyable:
Chain checklist:
Brief: goal [awareness / engagement / conversion], audience [who], platform [where].
Brand: colors [X], tone [Y].
Frames: main + [0–2] extras (lock before video).
Refs: [product/character – 3–5 angles] / none.
Clips: [2–4] × 3–5 s (I2V – image-to-video), not one long clip.
Audio: [voice first / bed only] + rights [licensed / demo].
Edit: cut + color + mix.
Check: brand | message | format | rights | AI label (C2PA / disclosure).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Before video, do you have at least one locked frame? Do you know whether sound will be voice-first or bed only?

sections.heading: Where to use this

slides.title: Image prompt basics
slides.subtitle: What to describe: subject, style, ratio

sections.heading: In short
sections.body: A good image prompt covers what is shown (subject, place, action), style (photoreal, illustration), ratio (e.g., 16:9, 1:1) and what to avoid.

sections.heading: Formula and three layers
sections.body: Image = Object + Context + Aesthetics (style). Layers: object (what is shown), context (place, action), aesthetics (style, light).

sections.heading: Minimum requirements
sections.body: At least 3–7 words; avoid vague words (“nice”, “interesting” with no context); use concrete nouns. A style keyword crowns the idea.

sections.heading: Do this now
sections.body: Open one image tool and copy the prompt below. Replace [DESCRIPTION] with your topic.

sections.heading: Copyable prompt
sections.body: Image prompt template – copy and fill [DESCRIPTION].
sections.copyable: Create an image: [DESCRIPTION]. Style: professional, bright, minimal. Ratio: 16:9. Do not add text inside the image.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Did the image match the description? If not – add place, lighting or style, or say “no text in the image”.

sections.heading: Why this works
sections.body: Start with “create an image” (or “generate an image”) plus a concrete ask – the tool then knows the task.

slides.title: Style and ratios for images
slides.subtitle: Style controls look; ratio controls format

sections.heading: In short
sections.body: Style: photorealistic, acrylic, 3D, drawing. Aspect ratio (frame width×height): 1:1 square, 16:9 wide, 9:16 vertical (stories).

sections.heading: Brand consistency
sections.body: So AI does not generate a random look, specify in the prompt: color system (e.g. deep blue + orange accent), typography (minimal or classic serif), tone (professional, friendly) and visual identity (corporate style, clean background).

sections.heading: Do this now
sections.body: Pick one style and one ratio. Write a 15+ word style header and do not rewrite it. Copy the lock below – one model for the whole series.

sections.heading: Copyable prompt
sections.body: Template with style and ratio fields.
sections.copyable:
Image: [WHAT IS SHOWN].
Style: [photorealistic / acrylic painting / minimal vector / 3D render].
Ratio: [1:1 / 16:9 / 9:16]. Language: neutral scene, no text in the image unless needed.

sections.heading: Copyable style lock
sections.body: 3–7 lines – repeat the same sentence in the series.
sections.copyable:
Style lock (do not swap the words): clean catalog shot, light from the left, white background, true product colors, readable label, no text on top.
Same product, same ratio, same label placement.
Model for this series: [one]. Do not switch mid-series.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Is the style header still verbatim (15+ words)? Same model for the whole series? Does the platform support the ratio?

slides.title: Product and character – the same look
slides.subtitle: 3–5 reference photos + a “same product” rule

sections.heading: In short
sections.body: A single prompt does not lock identity. In marketing you need 3–5 reference photos (different angles) and the rule “same product / same style / same colors” – otherwise the set drifts.

sections.heading: Reference lock – diagram
sections.body: Four steps – tap a stage. You will copy the rule in the Consistency lab.
sections.imageAlt: Reference lock: refs, rule, generate, QA

sections.heading: Brand / product sheet (minimum)
sections.body: (1) Hero / front view. (2) ¾ or side. (3) Flatlay or detail (label). (4) Optional – style / lighting ref.

sections.heading: Do this now
sections.body: Collect or generate at least 3 reference photos for your product or character. In the Consistency lab, tick refs and diagnose drift.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Do you have at least 3 angles as refs? If the set still drifts – use Consistency lab: Symptom | Fix and copy the rule. Avoid real people’s faces without consent.

recognitionExercise.title: Recognize style and ratios
recognitionExercise.task: Read 5 situations and choose the best answer for each one.
examples: You need a square LinkedIn post with a product image.
The same product should look like a premium catalog photo.
The hero image needs space for a headline on the left.
All campaign images must use the same colors and tone.
A Stories format needs a vertical frame.
explanations: A square social post uses a 1:1 ratio.
A premium catalog look is controlled mainly by style: light, texture, realism and tone.
Leaving space for a headline is a composition decision.
Repeating colors and tone protects brand consistency across images.
Stories, Reels and similar mobile formats usually use a vertical 9:16 ratio.

slides.title: Script for a short video
slides.subtitle: What happens, how long, what tone

sections.heading: In short
sections.body: A short video needs a clear script, tone and camera. Prefer 2–4 short clips (3–5 s) over one long try – lock frames before expensive video.

sections.heading: Framing and camera angle
sections.body: Framing changes emotion: eye-level, high angle, low angle, POV – write it in the prompt. Video models are strongest at motion and time, not inventing a full look from scratch.

sections.heading: Image-to-video chain
sections.body: Hero image / keyframe → I2V (Runway, Kling, Veo, Seedance, Sora) → edit. Sound first: if you will add voice-over, lock voice length first – then cut clips to the audio.

sections.heading: Do this now
sections.body: Write 2–3 sentences of script for one 3–5 s shot. Copy the template.

sections.heading: Prompt to copy
sections.body: Template for one short clip.
sections.copyable:
Clip 3–5 s (no longer).
Script: [what happens in this shot].
Camera: [slow push-in / side / stable / crane up].
Tone: [professional / dynamic / calm].
Start: image-to-video from hero keyframe. Same style, same colors.

sections.heading: Copyable chain – image → video
sections.body: Hero image first, then animation; for longer pieces use several keyframes.
sections.copyable:
1) Hero frame: [SUBJECT], [CONTEXT], style [STYLE], 16:9 or 9:16.
2) I2V 3–5 s from that frame: camera […], same product / same style.
(If you need longer – second keyframe, then edit.)

sections.heading: Copyable I2V cycle
sections.body: Change one variable – then watch the last frame.
sections.copyable:
Start: attach the keyframe. Keep identity and framing.
What does not change: [product / label / colors / light from the left].
The subject does: [one verb].
Camera: [one move]. No orbit, no tilt, no stacked moves.
Duration: 3 s first. Last frame: label readable, no new objects.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Did you write the invariants? Did you change only one thing? Did you watch the last second (label, fingers, crop)?

sections.heading: Same look across shots
sections.body: Same reference + “same product / same style”. Avoid real faces or voices without consent.

slides.title: I2V klipo generatorius
slides.subtitle: Image-to-video (I2V): keyframe → 3–5 s → camera → same style

content.tldr: In short: Describe the keyframe / scene, pick duration (3–5 s) and camera move. The system builds an I2V (image-to-video) prompt – copy it into Kling, Runway, Veo or Sora.
content.patikra: Does the prompt include a keyframe, 3 s first, one camera and one action? Did you watch the last second – label readable, no new objects? If you need a brand voice – keep the clip silent and write voice separately (do not stack Veo native sound on the same file).

slides.title: Edit after generation
slides.subtitle: AI = raw material; cut, color, mix

sections.heading: In short
sections.body: AI video is raw material, not the final deliverable. Professional practice: edit 3–5 s clips, color grade, text/overlay, mix audio, export for the platform (CapCut / Premiere).

sections.heading: Edit diagram
sections.body: Four steps – Cut → Grade → Mix → Export. Tap a stage.

sections.heading: Minimum checklist
sections.body: (1) Gather 2–4 clips to the script / VO. (2) Cut weak frames; hook in the first 1–2 s. (3) Keep colors consistent. (4) VO or bed + SFX. (5) Loudness guide ~−14 LUFS (music) / ~−16 (VO mix) – trust your ears. (6) Export 9:16 or 16:9.

sections.heading: Do this now
sections.body: Write a 4-line edit plan for your mini clip.

sections.heading: Copyable template
sections.body: Edit plan for 15–30 s.
sections.copyable:
Edit plan (15–30 s):
0–3 s: [hook clip]
3–8 s: [product / benefit]
8–15 s: [proof / detail]
End: [CTA frame + text]
Audio: [VO / bed] | rights: [licensed]

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Without AI “magic”, does the clip still read as a story? Does the bed drown the VO?

sections.heading: In short

Create a background music fragment, 30–60 seconds.
Mood: [calm / energetic]. Style: [acoustic / electronic / piano].
Tempo: [slow / medium]. No vocals. Use: [ads / presentation] – needs a commercial license.

sections.body: Voice-over template (ElevenLabs or similar).

Voiceover, [EN], tone [professional / friendly], tempo [calm].

No bed in the file – voice only. Mix with bed later.

sections.heading: Copyable voice card

Role: [who they speak to]. Tone: [warm / calm]. Keep the same tempo.
Glossary: [brand] = [how to say it].
First try 3 lines: hook / benefit / ask. Then the full script.
Bed: no vocal, quiet, leave room for the voice. License: commercial.

slides.title: Warm-up before the test
slides.subtitle: 3 questions before the graded test – not scored

questions.question: Before you generate a hero image, what should you choose first?
options: The campaign goal: awareness, engagement or conversion – then the visual
Only the tool, and leave the goal “as it comes”
Only the file name
Only the music BPM
questions.explanation: Strong: A/E/C (awareness / engagement / conversion) tells you what to emphasize in the image. If you missed it – go back to campaign goals.

questions.question: How do you keep the same product or character across several frames?
options: 3–5 reference photos from different angles and the rule “same product / same style”
One long prompt with no references, hoping the set will match
Switch tools after every frame
Specify only the file name
questions.explanation: Strong: a single prompt does not lock identity. If the set drifts – use reference photos and the “same product” rule.

questions.question: After the test, what should you do first in the project module?
options: One main image with a prompt and a short task note; video and audio if you want to join the pieces
Jump straight into editing a 3-minute film with no task note
Skip the image and go only to music
Wait for AI to choose the campaign goal
questions.explanation: First one image with a prompt. Video, audio and edit if you want to join the pieces. Do not burn time before you have a base result.

slides.title: Questions
slides.subtitle: Images, video, audio, media chain

testQuestions.question: What should a good image prompt include?
options: Describe only the lighting in detail and leave style “as it comes”
Subject, style, ratio and what to avoid
Name the tool and a seed number, with no subject
Write a long mood description with no format and no “what to avoid”
testQuestions.explanation: A good image prompt covers what is shown (subject, place), style (photoreal, illustration), ratio (16:9, 1:1) and what to avoid (e.g. text in the image).

testQuestions.scenarioContext: You need a LinkedIn post series: every image should look like one brand, and Stories should be vertical.
testQuestions.question: What must you specify in the prompt to reduce a chaotic brand look and hit the format?
options: Specify only a mood (“professional”) and leave the format to the tool
Brand colors, tone and ratios (e.g. 1:1 feed / 9:16 Stories)
Specify only the file name and duration, with no brand rules
Specify only the music tempo – the image will supposedly assemble itself
testQuestions.explanation: Brand consistency (colors, tone) plus clear platform ratios keeps the model from inventing a random style.

testQuestions.question: What should you specify for a short video?
options: Name only the tool (Kling or Runway) and hope the scene assembles itself
A script: what happens, how many seconds, and in what tone
Ask for “dynamic video” with no shots and no duration
Specify only 9:16 and leave the action empty
testQuestions.explanation: A short video needs a clear script: what happens, how long, and in what tone (professional, dynamic, calm).

testQuestions.question: What should you describe for music generation?
options: Specify only BPM and hope the mood appears
Mood, style, tempo and, if needed, instruments or voice
Ask for “nice music for an ad” with no style and no use case
Specify only duration (30 s) with no mood
testQuestions.explanation: Music generation needs mood (upbeat, calm), style (pop, acoustic), tempo (slow, mid) and, if needed, instruments or voice.

testQuestions.scenarioContext: You are planning a public campaign where an AI-made face or voice will look like a real person.
testQuestions.question: What should you check before publishing?
options: Only image sharpness and the color palette
Consent, copyright and deepfake risk
Only whether the face looks realistic enough
Only the social-network algorithm rules
testQuestions.explanation: A face or voice in an ad raises ethics and rights questions: consent, whose likeness, and the tool rules. If you miss this, review the risks slide.

testQuestions.question: You need a 15 s product ad from one marketing brief. Which generation chain is the most logical?
options: Video → brief → image → music
Brief → concept / prompt → hero image → video → voice / music → edit → QA
Music → publish → image → brief
Hero image → publish → video
testQuestions.explanation: A logical work process: first the brief and direction, then the image, then video and sound, then edit and a check. Generating the final video first or publishing without a check is expensive and chaotic.

testQuestions.scenarioContext: Your goal is a conversion ad in Instagram Stories. You need a hero image with a clear product and space for a headline.
testQuestions.question: Which prompt fits this situation best?
options: Create an attention-grabbing 9:16 image with no product – only emotion matters.
Create a vertical 9:16 product hero: [product] in the foreground, clean background, brand colors [X], headline space at the top, a call-to-action area at the bottom, no random text in the image.
Create a 1:1 image with lots of detail and text in the frame – product in the background.
Create an artistic 9:16 frame with no headline space – atmosphere only, product optional.
testQuestions.explanation: A conversion visual needs a clear format, the product, brand rules and space for copy. Pure emotion or abstract beauty fits awareness better.

testQuestions.scenarioContext: You want a short 5–8 s clip that keeps the same product look and colors as the campaign hero visual.
testQuestions.question: What is the safest path here?
options: Write only a generic text-to-video prompt and hope the style matches.
First generate the hero image / keyframe, then use it in an image-to-video tool and ask to keep the same style and colors.
Start from music and make the video with no script.
Generate a 1-minute video in one prompt, because longer is better.
testQuestions.explanation: An image-to-video chain helps keep the same style, object and colors. A long video in one prompt is better split into short, clear scenes.

testQuestions.question: Why prepare a storyboard or still frames before expensive video generation?
options: So the file gets larger and export becomes heavier
So you can check composition and scene logic before video, and cut wasted generations and cost
So you no longer need a brief and can publish right away
So you no longer need to check usage rights before publishing
testQuestions.explanation: Still frames lock the visual cheaply; the video model then works on motion. That cuts randomness and the cost of a usable clip.

testQuestions.question: What does an audio-first work process mean?
options: Video first, then any audio
Finish the VO (or background-music length) first, then cut / generate video to the sound rhythm
Only SFX, no music
Only a silent export
testQuestions.explanation: Audio-first: voice or background music sets the edit rhythm. If the sound drifts, the video feels disconnected.

testQuestions.scenarioContext: A client needs AI-generated background music for a paid YouTube ad.
testQuestions.question: What should you check before choosing a tool?
options: Whether the music is loud enough under the ad
Whether the license allows commercial use and monetization
Whether the tool has a free plan with no sign-up
Whether the track generates in under a minute
testQuestions.explanation: For a client and a paid ad, the license must allow commercial use and monetization. A demo or a fast file with no rights check is not enough.

testQuestions.question: What are C2PA / Content Credentials used for?
options: To increase image resolution before publishing
To record and pass on the origin of the content and its edit history
To shorten the prompt so the model makes fewer mistakes
To auto-correct colors to match the brand
testQuestions.explanation: C2PA / Content Credentials record origin: who made or changed the file, and how. A human-visible AI label is a separate disclosure practice; a persistent watermark (e.g. SynthID) is another layer, not C2PA itself.

sections.heading: In short

sections.copyable:
You are a content-chain assistant. Topic: [DESCRIBE].
1) Task: goal (A/E/C), audience, platform, ratios.
2) Frames: 2–3 frames (what, style, what to avoid).
3) Video or sound first: if video – image-to-video from the hero; if audio – voice / SFX / music + pacing.
4) Rights: commercial license; faces/voices – consent.
5) AI label (C2PA): Content Credentials or a human-visible AI label.
Output: checklist table (step | status | risk) + 1 next action.

sections.heading: Check

content.template: Keyframe: [WHAT IS SHOWN]. Setting: [CONTEXT]. Style: [STYLE]. Brand colors: [X]. Ratio: [1:1 / 16:9 / 9:16]. Leave space for a headline if needed.

steps.title: Choose or create a keyframe
steps.description: Same image works – go to video. Need another – paste the prompt into an image tool.

slides.title: Scenario: Short video
slides.subtitle: A 3–5 s clip from the keyframe

content.scenarioDescription: Turn the keyframe into a 3 s I2V clip: one camera, one action. Paste the prompt into a video tool (Runway, Kling, Veo or similar).

taskFrame.task: Generate a 3 s I2V clip from the keyframe: one camera, one action.
taskFrame.doneWhen: You watched the last second: label readable, no new objects, you changed only one thing. If the tool accepts an end frame – you attached it; first = keyframe, last = what must remain at the end.

scenario.narrativeLead: Use the I2V cycle: invariants + last-frame check, not only “did the style hold”.

content.template:
Start: attach the keyframe. Keep identity and framing.
What does not change: [product / label / colors / light from the left].
The subject does: [one verb].
Camera: [one move]. No orbit, no tilt, no stacked moves.
Duration: 3 s first. Last frame: label readable, no new objects.
If the tool supports it: also attach an end frame (what must remain at the end).
content.templateLabel: Prompt – paste into a video tool

steps.title: Generate a 3 s clip and watch the last frame
steps.description: Artifact: video file or link + prompt. Done when the last second is clean. If the tool accepts an end frame – attach it.

slides.title: Scenario: Voice or bed
slides.subtitle: Write for the ear + 3 anchor lines

content.scenarioDescription: Write for the ear: glossary + 3 anchor lines, then the full voice. Bed after the voice. One line: can you use it publicly?

taskFrame.task: Try 3 anchor lines at the same tempo, then the full voice.
taskFrame.doneWhen: Tempo and pronunciation stayed the same; the bed leaves room for the voice; rights are marked.

scenario.narrativeLead: Drift is tempo and pronunciation, not a “bad voice”. Try 3 lines first. Bed leaves room for the voice.

content.template:
Role: [who they speak to]. Tone: [warm / calm]. Keep the same tempo.
Glossary: [brand] = [how to say it].
First try 3 lines: hook / benefit / ask. Then the full script.
Bed: no vocal, quiet, leave room for the voice. Rights: commercial.
content.templateLabel: Prompt – paste into a voice tool

steps.title: Try 3 anchor lines, then the full voice
steps.description: Save the file or link, the prompt, and the glossary. Bed comes after the voice.

slides.title: Scenario: Edit
slides.subtitle: 15–30 s from 2–4 clips

content.scenarioDescription: Join image, video and audio into a 15–30 s whole. Use an edit tool (CapCut or similar). This is a plan, not a long prompt.

taskFrame.task: Assemble a 15–30 s clip: hook in the first 1–2 s, then export.
taskFrame.doneWhen: You have an export, rights marked, an AI label, and a CPI note (how many tries).

scenario.narrativeLead: AI gives the raw clips. Hook in the first 1–2 seconds. Before export, mark rights and an AI label.

content.template:
Edit plan (15–30 s):
0–3 s: [hook]
3–8 s: [product / benefit]
8–15 s: [detail]
End: [CTA]
Audio: [voice / bed] | rights: [licensed]
AI label: made with [tool]. CPI note: [N retries].
content.templateLabel: Edit plan – use in an edit tool
